subject: DPA redline Q&A: locality carveouts, snapshot retention & certified deletion
messages:
From: Danielle Morris <danielle.morris@globex.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aaron Li <aaron.li@globex.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2029 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood DPA — locality & deletion redlines

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks for sending the draft DPA. Attached are Globex's redlines (DPA_Globex_redlines.docx) — the main asks are below. We tried to keep changes focused to the residency and deletion sections but there are a few consequential carveouts we need clarity on.

Key points:
- Residency: Globex needs an explicit guarantee that EU customer data (as defined in Appendix A) will be stored in EU-located physical infrastructure. We understand replication for resilience, but onshore mirrors must be optional and contractually resourced.
- Backup / snapshot retention: we can't accept indefinite backup retention. Request: backups and snapshots containing EU customer data must be deleted within 30 days after primary data deletion, with a documented process for certified erasure.
- Certified deletion: request language that Redwood will provide a certified deletion statement for certified erasure events (standardized template).
- Cross-border access: any cross-border access for debugging/maintenance must be logged and subject to customer approval unless required by law.
- Lawful access / exceptions: we accept law enforcement carveouts but want notice and narrow scope where permitted.

Can we get Redwood's position on the 30-day backup window and the certified deletion commitment? If you prefer, we can set a call to walk through our redlines — Aaron and I are available next week (Mon/Tue morning PT).

Thanks,
Danielle

--
Danielle Morris

Globex Corp

Subject: Re: Redwood DPA — locality & deletion redlines

Hi Danielle — thanks for the redlines and the clear summary. Appreciate you calling out the high-priority items. I pulled in Marissa (legal) and Jonas (data privacy/product) so we can propose concrete language.

Quick, high-level responses before a deeper pass:
- Residency: we can support customer-controlled locality for primary data (EU, US, APAC) — customers can select region at onboarding and we will pin primary storage accordingly. For resilience, we use geographically separated replicas; we are open to contractually limiting cross-region mirrors for regulated customers when feasible, and to documenting when mirrors are used.
- Backup/snapshot retention: 30 days for backups is aggressive relative to our current operational model. Operational snapshots and backups are typically retained for 45 days to allow for recovery and incident investigations. We can propose 45 days for EU data backups with procedural guarantees for prompt deletion, plus an option for customers to request expedited certified deletion in specific cases.
- Certified deletion: we can provide a standardized certificate-of-deletion template for erasure requests. There are some limitations around third-party backup providers and immutable media; we'll mark those exceptions clearly in the template.
- Cross-border access and logging: we can require explicit customer consent for non-routine cross-border access and provide detailed logging for those events. Routine operational actions performed within approved regions will be covered by the residency guarantees.

If that high-level compromise works, we'll return redlined contract text and the deletion certificate template. Happy to take the call Tue 19 Mar at 9:00 AM PT — does that work for your team?

Best,
Karthik
Head of Product, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Karthik / Jonas —

Following our sync, I drafted suggested contract language to respond to Globex. Below are the primary edits I recommend; I'll attach a PDF with the redline. We should keep the optics conciliatory but protect operational requirements.

Proposed language (high level):
1) Residency guarantee: "Redwood will store Customer Primary Data within the geographical region selected by Customer (EU, US, APAC). Redwood may maintain replicas for resilience; replicas will only be placed outside the selected region where necessary for operational availability, and only after providing Customer with prior written notice and an option to opt-into mirrored deployment for an additional fee."

2) Backups & snapshots: "Backups and snapshots containing Customer Primary Data will be retained for a standard period of forty-five (45) days following deletion of the corresponding Primary Data, after which Redwood will schedule deletion. In cases where Customer requires expedited removal, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide a certificate of deletion within thirty (30) days of Customer's validated request, subject to any technical constraints on immutable storage media."

3) Certified deletion: attach standardized Certificate of Deletion template; include a materials-and-processes appendix describing exceptions (e.g., immutable WORM storage, third-party archival providers).

4) Cross-border access & logging: "Non-routine cross-border access to Customer Primary Data will require Customer's prior written approval; all cross-border access events will be recorded and made available in an audit log within the Redwood Console for thirty (30) days by default and for preservation as otherwise agreed."

5) Lawful access: narrow the notice window where permissible, but include a transparency commitment to provide notice unless prohibited by binding law.

I'm attaching redwood_dpa_response_20290318.pdf with the redline + the certificate template. If Karthik likes this, we should send the redlines back and offer the call Tue 9 AM PT.

Thanks for the quick turn. The 45-day backup window and the certificate-of-deletion template look reasonable as a starting point. A few clarifications before we finalize:

- Can you explicitly call out "EU Primary Data" in the backup clause so there's no ambiguity about scope?
- We need confirmation that cross-border access logs include the actor, purpose, and timestamp, and that those logs are exportable via the Console or delivered on request.
- Please confirm the SLA for producing a certificate-of-deletion once an expedited request is validated (you mentioned 30 days; we want that in the appendix).

If you can confirm those items in a final draft I can get this over to procurement/legal for an expedited review. We're OK to sign once the language is explicit and the DocuSign link is prepared.
